starting_points.name: Phoenix browser application with LiveView and PostgreSQL
starting_points.when: A new connected browser application uses this profile. Generate the skeleton before adding application code.
steps: Read the repository README, runtime pins and existing mix.exs/mix.lock first. Existing applications keep their structure; do not regenerate over them.
Choose a local source workspace and a new destination. Replace my_app with the chosen snake_case application name throughout these examples.
Install a compatible Erlang/OTP and Elixir pair using official installation guidance; check the chosen Phoenix release requirements. Set up PostgreSQL access for development and tests.
Check installed tools. Install Hex only if missing, and install the Phoenix archive only if missing or deliberately changing its version. Check installed generator help before choosing switches.
Generate the project, respond to the dependency-install prompt, then enter my_app. Review the generated README, mix.exs aliases, configuration and any agent guidance.

Configure database credentials outside committed secrets. Inspect the generated mix setup alias before running it; it can fetch dependencies, create/migrate the database and build assets. Resolve failures in place and retain their output.

commands.purpose: Inspect the active Elixir and Erlang/OTP versions
Install Hex only when missing; review the installation prompt

commands.cwd: chosen local workspace; only if installer is missing or a deliberate update is needed
commands.purpose: Install the Phoenix generator; select/record a compatible version according to project policy
Record the installed Phoenix generator version

commands.cwd: parent directory of the new my_app directory
commands.purpose: Generate the Phoenix application, including LiveView and asset defaults

commands.cwd: my_app project root, after inspecting the generated alias and configuring local database access

notes: LiveView is included by the normal Phoenix generator. Keep HTML and assets for this browser path.
Dependency installation is interactive by default; installed help documents --install and --no-install. These examples do not request a Git commit.
Use --no-agents-md only for an explicit repository instruction policy; preserve the generated guidance in its maintained README-linked owner when that policy requires it.

starting_points.name: Phoenix JSON API application
starting_points.when: The deliverable is an HTTP API with a separate client and does not need generated browser UI.
steps: Use the runtime, Hex, Phoenix archive and PostgreSQL prerequisite checks from the browser starting point.
Generate into a new destination; configure the database, inspect the generated setup alias and run it from the project root.
Select mailer, dashboard, Ecto and other omissions separately from actual requirements. Do not remove persistence simply because the interface is JSON.

commands.cwd: parent directory of the new my_app directory
commands.purpose: Generate an API skeleton without HTML views or asset build tools

notes: --no-html disables the generated LiveView setup; this is an alternative to the browser starting point.
--no-ecto changes what resource generators can provide. Use it only when the application truly does not need Ecto; inspect --no-context handling for later generators.
Browser authentication scaffolding is not an API-token or external identity implementation. Choose API authentication explicitly.

starting_points.name: Plain Mix library or supervised OTP service
starting_points.when: The project needs Elixir without a Phoenix web application. Choose the variant from process-lifecycle requirements.
steps: Verify compatible Elixir/Erlang and Mix; choose a new source destination. Replace my_library or my_service with the selected snake_case name.
For a library with no owned supervision tree, use mix new. For an application that owns long-lived processes, use mix new --sup.
Run only the selected creation command. Enter its generated directory, preserve its scaffold and implement application behavior after generation.

commands.cwd: parent directory of the new my_library directory
commands.purpose: Generate a plain Elixir project without an application callback/supervisor

commands.cwd: parent directory of the new my_service directory
commands.purpose: Alternative: generate an OTP application callback and supervision tree

notes: --sup is conditional, not a universal Elixir requirement. Do not hand-write mix.exs, formatter, test helper or supervision boilerplate when Mix supplies the appropriate base.
Use --umbrella only for a justified multi-application boundary; do not introduce it as a default.

follow_up_generators.name: Phoenix authentication
follow_up_generators.when: Application-owned browser accounts are required, after Phoenix setup.
notes: Run mix help phx.gen.auth first; substitute the context/schema/table deliberately. --live selects LiveView views; --no-live is the controller-view alternative.
Follow the generated routing/configuration instructions, fetch new dependencies with mix deps.get, inspect migrations and apply them to the intended local database with mix ecto.migrate.
Review delivery, scope and authorization requirements. Generated email authentication assumes email-account ownership; preserve its token-revocation and confirmation safeguards when customizing.
Do not run multiple auth generators blindly: scopes and browser-pipeline assignments can conflict. Use external identity integration when that is the actual requirement.

follow_up_generators.name: LiveView resource
follow_up_generators.when: A new browser CRUD resource should follow Phoenix conventions.

commands.run: mix phx.gen.live Catalog Product products name:string

notes: Example names/fields are substitutions, not a domain prescription. Run mix help phx.gen.live and decide context boundaries before generating.
This generates the context/schema/migration and LiveView files/tests. Apply the printed router changes and inspect/migrate the local database.
Preserve configured scope behavior and add permission/domain checks. --no-context implies --no-schema and leaves implementation work, including failing generated tests, to complete.
Use this or the other resource variants below; do not generate the same resource repeatedly with each variant.

follow_up_generators.name: Controller HTML resource
follow_up_generators.when: The resource uses conventional server-rendered controllers/templates rather than LiveView.

commands.run: mix phx.gen.html Catalog Product products name:string

notes: Alternative to phx.gen.live, requiring the HTML components omitted by --no-html. Run installed task help first.
Review generated context, schema, migration, controller/templates and tests; complete the printed routing instructions and migration steps.

follow_up_generators.name: JSON API resource
follow_up_generators.when: The resource is exposed as JSON.

commands.run: mix phx.gen.json Catalog Product products name:string

notes: Alternative to HTML/LiveView resource generation. Run installed task help; review generated controller/JSON rendering, context, schema, migration and tests.
Complete printed routing instructions and migrations. Add actual API authentication/authorization, validation and response-contract tests.

follow_up_generators.name: Domain context without web UI
follow_up_generators.when: The application needs a new domain resource/API boundary without generated HTTP or LiveView files.

commands.run: mix phx.gen.context Catalog Product products name:string

notes: Run installed task help and review context boundaries. The generator adds schema, migration and context tests.
An existing context can be extended; inspect the merge prompt instead of blindly accepting it. Choose --no-schema only when intentionally supplying that implementation.

follow_up_generators.name: Ecto schema without context scaffolding
follow_up_generators.when: A schema and migration are needed within a deliberately maintained domain boundary.
notes: Run installed task help; choose attribute types, references, ID strategy and table names explicitly.
Review changesets and migration constraints/indexes. This generator does not provide the enclosing context API or authorization.

follow_up_generators.name: Ecto migration
follow_up_generators.when: An existing persisted resource requires a schema change, without duplicating its resource generator.
notes: Requires an Ecto repository configured under :ecto_repos, or choose it with --repo. Run installed task help before use.

Edit the generated timestamped migration; review reversibility, data and locking effects. Apply it to the intended local database, then test the changed behavior. Do not rewrite migrations already deployed to shared databases.

follow_up_generators.name: Phoenix release helpers
notes: Run installed task help first. Review migration/server scripts and runtime configuration before building the release.
Use --docker only when a container is required; inspect generated base-image/runtime versions and add any external asset package-manager steps.
Generation/build success does not prove deployment, migrations, backup/restore or runtime compatibility.

integration_steps: After completing the selected starting point, read its generated README, mix.exs, mix.lock and runtime pins. Preserve the chosen plain Mix or Phoenix architecture; the following Phoenix integrations apply only when Phoenix is present.

For a Phoenix application, inspect and complete the generated setup alias after configuring development/test database access. Keep credentials outside committed secrets; follow the generator output when a selected omission means an alias or integration is unavailable.

If dependency guidance synchronization is useful, add usage_rules as a development dependency, choose the relevant dependency rules in mix.exs and review mix usage_rules.sync output. Preserve maintained generated guidance; an explicit README-only policy may configure a README-linked alternate file such as docs/dependency-rules.md.

If Phoenix browser accounts are required, complete the authentication follow-up recipe, review its generated instructions and configure transactional email delivery. Keep local/test delivery adapters in their intended environments; verify scopes and permission checks for application operations.

If durable background jobs are required, follow the installed Oban version’s installation and migration instructions, supervise Oban and configure bounded queues. Use supported persistence and idempotent workers; test retry and duplicate-effect handling. A Task is suitable only for explicitly disposable work.

Add development and test checks selected for this project. Formatter, compiler warnings and ExUnit apply to plain Mix applications; Ecto SQL Sandbox, LiveViewTest, Sobelow and other Phoenix-specific checks require their corresponding dependencies and application architecture.

For Phoenix applications that need real-browser verification, install/configure PhoenixTest.Playwright or the selected browser suite with its matching JavaScript dependency and browser binaries. Configure the test endpoint and SQL sandbox as documented; server-side LiveView tests do not establish browser JavaScript or visual correctness.

Run the applicable verification commands and actual application flows, fixing failures in place and retaining evidence. Skip tools whose dependency was not selected rather than claiming their checks passed; do not regenerate over existing work to hide failures.

For deployment qualification, select the intended host and runtime configuration. In Phoenix applications follow the release-helper recipe; build production assets only when the selected application has assets. Build a release compatible with the target OS, architecture and native dependencies.

Before claiming production readiness, rehearse startup, migrations and any applicable reconnect/job-retry behavior on the selected host. Establish secrets, TLS, backups, restore and rollback ownership; a generated release or passing local tests do not establish those outcomes.

Completion: record exact runtime/dependency versions, the application lockfile, selected generation/integration steps, check results and observed flows in README-linked evidence. State any untested deployment or native-mobile paths explicitly.
preserve: Keep generated mix.exs aliases, .formatter.exs, tests/helpers, configuration, runtime supervision and project documentation as the starting base; make deliberate, reviewable changes rather than recreating the scaffold by hand.
Preserve the complete generated .gitignore and add project/platform entries such as .DS_Store as supplements. Do not claim every generator version already ignores macOS metadata.
Retain dependency lockfiles for application reproducibility according to repository policy. Keep credentials, build outputs and dependency caches out of commits.
Existing project conventions and maintained README-linked guidance remain authoritative; generator commands are for new projects or deliberate scoped additions, not destructive replacement.
Record the generator command, versions, selected switches and reasons for deviations with the project setup evidence.
verification: Before generation, inspect installed mix help for each selected task and check the chosen runtime/generator requirements against installed versions; unversioned documentation can describe a newer release.

Inspect the generated files and pending repository diff, including hidden files. Check that formatter configuration, tests/helpers, ignore rules and required application supervision are present for the selected variant.
Run mix format --check-formatted, mix compile --warnings-as-errors and mix test from the generated project root after dependency/database setup. Repair failures in place and record actual results.

For Phoenix browser applications, run mix phx.server and inspect the actual local page and generated flows; for APIs, exercise the intended requests. A server process starting is not a completed interaction check.

Use git status --short --untracked-files=all and git check-ignore -v .DS_Store _build deps to review the selected ignore rules. In a disposable copy or separate index, inspect what staging all files would include; never alter the user index merely to test hygiene.
Confirm generated authentication/scopes and application operations reject unauthorized access; generated CRUD does not settle domain permissions.
This record is documentation-reviewed only. No application generator, setup command, database operation, test suite or release build was executed for this research.
